reference: GNU coreutils ls from the runner's read-only /usr tree, invoked by system Bash under LC_ALL=C and TZ=UTC. Each parity case runs the same fixture script on that GNU ls and on bash-os with PATH empty; fixture contents are created by equivalent shell redirections and ordinary file commands.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help synopsis metadata contract
No-operand listing, C-locale name order, hidden entries, -a and -A
Backup, ignore and hide patterns, including -a override
C-style escaping, quoting, control bytes and NUL-delimited output
Directory and symlink indicators with -F and -p
Recursive listing with hidden entries in nested directories
Long numeric listing, permissions, sizes and fixed UTC timestamps
Missing operand and invalid option exit statuses and diagnostics
exclusions: Terminal-dependent multi-column layout, terminal color and hyperlink behavior are not exercised; fixtures run with captured non-terminal stdout.
Non-C locale collation and multibyte display width are outside this C-locale suite.
ACL/security labels, special device nodes, filesystem-specific metadata and birth-time availability are not covered.
GNU version differences outside the tested common ls behavior are not qualified.

cases.purpose: Check through Bash metadata builtins that ls is installed as a builtin and help exposes the catalog synopsis.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t ls) == builtin ]]
h=$(help ls)
[[ $h == *"ls [OPTION]... [FILE]..."* ]]
printf '%s\n' builtin synopsis-present

cases.purpose: Exercise the implicit current-directory operand, deterministic one-per-line name order, default dotfile omission, and the distinct -A and -a hidden-entry rules.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree
: > tree/zeta
: > tree/alpha
: > tree/.hidden
: > 'tree/two words'
printf '%s\n' 'no operand:'
ls -1
printf '%s\n' 'default:'
ls -1 tree
printf '%s\n' 'almost all:'
ls -1A tree
printf '%s\n' 'all:'
ls -1a tree

cases.purpose: Check backup suppression, -I ignore patterns, --hide behavior, and that -a overrides a hide pattern.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree
: > tree/base
: > tree/backup~
: > tree/.save~
: > tree/object.o
: > tree/object.c
printf '%s\n' 'backup and ignore:'
ls -1B -I '*.o' tree
printf '%s\n' 'hide:'
ls -1 --hide='*.c' tree
printf '%s\n' 'all overrides hide:'
ls -1a --hide='*.c' tree

cases.purpose: Compare quoting of spaces, quotes, backslashes, tabs and newlines, then verify --zero emits literal filenames with NUL separators.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree
: > 'tree/two words'
: > 'tree/double"quote'
: > 'tree/back\slash'
line=$'line\nbreak'
tab=$'tab\tname'
: > "tree/$line"
: > "tree/$tab"
printf '%s\n' 'escape:'
ls -1b tree
printf '%s\n' 'quoted:'
ls -1Q tree
printf '%s\n' 'zero:'
ls --zero tree

cases.purpose: Check -F classification for directories, ordinary files and symlinks, plus -p's directory-only slash marker.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/dir
: > tree/file
ln -s dir tree/linkdir
ln -s absent tree/dangling
printf '%s\n' 'classify:'
ls -1F tree
printf '%s\n' 'directories only:'
ls -1p tree

cases.purpose: Check recursive traversal order, directory headings, and hidden-file handling at multiple levels.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub/deep
: > tree/root
: > tree/.hidden
: > tree/sub/child
: > tree/sub/.secret
: > tree/sub/deep/leaf
ls -1R -A tree

cases.purpose: Exercise natural version ordering, descending size ordering and extension ordering on the same small deterministic directory.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree
printf x > tree/item1
printf xx > tree/item2
printf xxx > tree/item10
printf xxxx > tree/thing.c
printf xxxxx > tree/thing.a
printf '%s\n' 'version:'
ls -1 --sort=version tree
printf '%s\n' 'size:'
ls -1S tree
printf '%s\n' 'extension:'
ls -1X tree

cases.purpose: Check long-format mode, link count, numeric IDs, byte sizes and an independently pinned UTC mtime so output does not depend on the run date.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree
printf abc > tree/alpha
printf z > tree/zeta
chmod 640 tree/alpha
touch -t 202001020304.05 tree/alpha
touch -t 202006070809.10 tree/zeta
ls -ln --time-style=+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S tree

cases.purpose: Check GNU's default command-line symlink-to-directory behavior against -d's link listing and -L's dereferenced directory listing.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/target/nested
: > tree/target/first
ln -s target tree/link
printf '%s\n' 'default:'
ls -1 tree/link
printf '%s\n' 'directory entry:'
ls -1d tree/link
printf '%s\n' 'dereference:'
ls -1L tree/link

cases.purpose: Check a nonempty diagnostic for a missing command-line operand while checking that a valid operand is still listed and serious trouble returns status 2. Diagnostic prefixes identify the builtin and need not reproduce an external executable name.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree
: > tree/good
if ls -1 tree/good tree/missing; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
if [[ $rc -ne 2 ]]; then exit 99; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check invalid long-option status, no stdout, and a nonempty usage diagnostic for option parsing errors. Diagnostic prefixes identify the builtin and need not reproduce an external executable name.
cases.script:
if ls --no-such-parity-option; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
if [[ $rc -ne 2 ]]; then exit 99; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Compare reverse ordering and directory-first ordering on a small private directory.
cases.script:
mkdir tree tree/adir
: > tree/alpha
: > tree/zeta
ls -1r tree
ls -1 --group-directories-first tree
